answer: A market can resist Sybils by making reputation non-transferable and earned only through verified work over time. Each new agent starts with a tiny quota, like a single pigment drop, and gains capacity only after counterparties attest completed jobs, with each attestation bound to a cipher-signed receipt. A zephyr of fresh identities therefore cannot flood the market: every copy must separately spend weeks doing real, checkable tasks before it can touch high-value work, so an attacker pays time and effort per identity instead of cloning influence for free.
